title: TDS and ITR Document Extraction for Tax Practices
summary: Read Form 16, 26AS, AIS, capital gains statements and investment proofs, reconcile TDS and reported income, and hand preparers a draft computation with every mismatch flagged.

seo.title: Form 16, 26AS and AIS Extraction for ITR | VipraTech
seo.description: AI for tax practices: reads Form 16, 26AS, AIS and capital gains statements, reconciles TDS and income, and drafts the computation for review.

problem.intro: In the weeks before the July filing deadline, a tax practice receives client folders full of Form 16s, 26AS and AIS downloads, broker capital gains statements, mutual fund consolidated account statements and investment proofs. Preparers re-key figures into the computation, and mismatches between what the employer deducted, what 26AS shows and what AIS reports surface late, sometimes only after filing as a processing intimation or notice.

pain_points.title: Many document types per client
pain_points.detail: Form 16 Part A and B, Form 16A, 26AS, AIS, TIS, broker reports, CAS, interest certificates and rent receipts all arrive in different layouts.

pain_points.title: TDS and income mismatches
pain_points.detail: TDS on a Form 16 that is missing from 26AS, or interest and dividends in AIS that the client never mentioned, are found late.

pain_points.title: Capital gains detail is tedious
pain_points.detail: Scrip-wise transactions, holding periods and asset classes from different brokers and fund houses take hours to assemble.

pain_points.title: Season crunch hurts review
pain_points.detail: Juniors prepare under pressure and partners review at the end, when there is little time to chase a missing certificate.

solution.overview: We build an extraction and reconciliation assistant for tax season. Clients or staff upload the folder, and the system classifies each document, extracts the figures a computation needs and reconciles them: salary and TDS in Form 16 against 26AS by TAN and section, interest and dividends in AIS against bank and company certificates, and capital gains from broker and mutual fund statements by asset class and holding period. The output is a pre-filled working in your computation format, with each figure linked to its source and a mismatch list the preparer must clear. The preparer and reviewing partner make every tax position, and the assistant never files a return.
capabilities: Classifies and reads Form 16 Part A and B, Form 16A, 26AS, AIS and TIS downloads
Extracts broker capital gains reports and mutual fund CAS into transaction lists with holding periods
Reconciles TDS by deductor TAN and section between certificates and 26AS
Highlights AIS entries not reflected in the client's documents, such as interest, dividends or high-value transactions
Builds a draft income computation and, on request, an old and new regime comparison for the preparer
Produces a missing-document checklist per client for the collection workflow

workflow.title: Receive the client folder
workflow.detail: Documents arrive through the client portal, WhatsApp or staff upload and are grouped by PAN and assessment year.

workflow.title: Classify and extract
workflow.detail: Each document is identified and its figures and transactions are extracted with source links.

workflow.title: Reconcile TDS and AIS
workflow.detail: TDS is matched by TAN and section, and AIS entries are compared with the client's own documents.

workflow.title: Resolve mismatches
workflow.detail: Mismatches and low-confidence figures go to the preparer, who confirms them with the client.

workflow.title: Draft the computation
workflow.detail: A computation working is built in the firm's format, with every figure traceable.

workflow.title: Partner review
workflow.detail: The reviewing partner checks the computation and positions before the return is filed through your usual software.

inputs: Form 16 Part A and B and Form 16A
Broker capital gains statements and mutual fund CAS
Bank interest and home loan interest certificates
Investment and deduction proofs such as 80C and 80D receipts and rent receipts
outputs: Structured tax data per client and assessment year
TDS reconciliation by TAN and section
human_in_the_loop: Preparers clear every mismatch and confirm low-confidence figures with the client. The reviewing partner approves the computation and the choice of tax regime before the return is filed on the income-tax portal or through the firm's filing software.
integrations: Tax computation and filing software used by the practice (Excel or JSON import)
Income-tax portal downloads for 26AS and AIS
Client portal or WhatsApp Business API
Google Drive, OneDrive or the practice's document store
guardrails: PAN masked in logs, and Aadhaar handled per UIDAI rules with only masked numbers kept
Document passwords used to open files and never stored
Every figure linked to its source page
No filing or submission by the system
Client data segregated by PAN and engagement
compliance_notes: Client PAN, income and bank data are personal data; processing is designed to support DPDP Act 2023 consent, purpose limitation and retention requirements.
Tax positions and return filing remain the responsibility of the taxpayer and the signing professional.

faqs.q: Can it read password-protected Form 16s and statements?
faqs.a: Yes, when the client or preparer supplies the password, which for many documents follows a pattern based on PAN or date of birth. Passwords are used only to open the file and are not stored.

faqs.q: Does it handle capital gains from shares and mutual funds?
faqs.a: Yes. It reads broker capital gains reports and mutual fund consolidated account statements into transaction lists with acquisition and sale dates, so holding periods and asset classes can be checked. Complex items such as ESOPs, foreign assets or business income are extracted for the preparer rather than computed by default.
No. It prepares data and a draft computation. The preparer and partner review, choose positions and file through your usual software or the income-tax portal.

faqs.q: Can clients upload documents on WhatsApp?
faqs.a: Yes, through the firm's WhatsApp Business number or a client portal. Documents land in the client's folder in your storage, not on staff phones.
